The commissioning agent has found eleven that are the same test — and that isn’t the worst of it.  ⚑ RV-160: installation methods are the installer’s; verification is the commissioning agent’s. RV-161: figures illustrative. Some choices run on a clock.

items.title: Pull Test
items.stakes: Forty-eight cable certifications, all PASS. Eleven are the same test. And the long south group was pulled far too hard.
items.reward: Every link proved for real — and a report you can trust next time.

objectives.text: Decide what to do with the report
Decide what happens to the failing links

items.alt: The site trailer; Nkechi, the commissioning agent, holds a thick report; Maya reads the page she's pulled out.

bubbles.text: Forty-eight passes. Eleven of them are the same test.

items.caption: Acceptance meeting on Friday.

lines.text: Sixty-one point four metres. Eleven times. In rooms on three different floors.
Then we don't have forty-eight tests. We have thirty-seven and a photocopier.

items.text: ✦ UX RULE #75 · AVERY'S LENS  Evidence must belong to what it proves  A test result is only evidence if it can be traced to the thing it names — raw data, a time, a witness.  Forty-eight PASS reports. Eleven of them were one test saved eleven times, and nobody could tell from the summary page.

items.alt: A certification sheet: five sample rows; three consecutive links, L-117, L-118 and L-119, highlighted in red with identical length 61.4 m and identical margin 4.1 dB; notes: eleven results identical, saved within 90 seconds; the south group pulled by winch at about 400 N on cable rated about 110 N.
items.caption: Real runs are never twins.

items.prompt: 09:30. The LV sub says the report is fine and wants acceptance on Friday. What do you do?

hints.text: What would prove which link each result belongs to?

options.label: Accept it — it says 48 PASS
options.result: Nkechi: “Then you're accepting eleven tests that never happened.”
options.fail: Evidence must trace to the thing it names.

options.label: Ask the LV sub for the tester's raw files and have Nkechi witness a retest of a sample, including the eleven
options.result: The raw file holds one measurement saved eleven times; the witnessed sample is booked for Tuesday.

options.label: Reject the whole installation
options.result: Thirty-seven good links condemned with eleven bad reports.

options.label: Borrow a tester and retest them yourself
options.result: Nkechi: “Their links, their test. I witness. You write what it must prove.”
options.consequence: Doing the installer's work — and the verifier's.

items.title: Eleven twins.
items.body: The tester's raw file for links L-117 to L-127 holds a single measurement, saved under eleven link IDs in ninety seconds. Eleven links — almost a quarter of the installation — were never tested. The summary page couldn't tell you; the raw file could.
items.label: Test: how much of the installation — and what proves which link a result belongs to?

items.title: Too hard a pull.
items.body: Nkechi witnesses a retest of twelve links from the long south group to the broadcast room. Five fail near-end crosstalk. The pulling log: fourteen cables in one winch pull, set to about 400 newtons. The data sheet stapled behind it: maximum pulling tension about 110. The jackets at the south pull box carry stretch marks.
items.label: Test: how far over — and will re-terminating fix it?

items.prompt: Tuesday. Five of twelve fail. What do you require?
items.risk: Damaged links hidden in the walls — or weeks lost replacing good ones.
timeout: The sub asks for a waiver in writing.
Friday's meeting has five failures on the table and no plan.

hints.text: Which links share the cause — and who chooses the method?

options.label: Accept the five with a waiver — they're nearly in spec
options.result: The broadcast room drops frames on day one.
options.fail: Never waive a failed test into a finished wall.

options.label: The fourteen winch-pulled links replaced using a method that stays within their rated tension — the sub's choice of method — and all 48 retested, witnessed by Nkechi
options.result: The sub re-pulls by hand with a tension-limited grip on Wednesday; all 48 pass, witnessed, raw files attached.
options.consequence: Their method, your limits, her witness.

options.label: Re-terminate only the five failures
options.result: Three still fail; two pass by a hair and fail next winter.
options.consequence: The damage is in the cable, not at the ends.

options.label: Replace every cable in the building
options.result: Weeks lost for thirty-four good links.

items.title: The cable that was pushed too hard
items.body: In August 1858 the first telegraph cable across the Atlantic carried messages for a few weeks. Its signals were faint, and one of the project's electricians raised the voltage — to around two thousand volts — to force them through. The insulation failed and the cable went silent. The next cables were run within their limits, and they lasted.

items.alt: The certification sheet after the retest: every sample row with a different real length and margin, all PASS with ticks, L-140 re-pulled; notes: 48 links retested and witnessed with raw files; south group re-pulled within rated tension.
items.caption: Forty-eight real tests.

items.prompt: Some designers hate me turning up to watch tests. Slows everything down, they say.

options.label: “Watching is the test. I'll write it into the spec so nobody can say you slowed them down.”
options.reply: Then I'll bring the good coffee.

options.label: “What do you need from me to witness properly?”
options.reply: Raw files, a schedule, and a sub who knows I'm coming.

items.title: L-117 … L-127 · 10:41:02–10:42:31
items.body: The tester's file list: L-117 to L-127, saved 10:41:02 to 10:42:31. Eleven links in three rooms on two floors, ninety seconds. The file sizes are identical.

unknown: What the fiber report looks like

hints.text: What would have caught the eleven on day one?

options.label: Trust the summaries — this was a one-off
options.result: The fiber certification arrives next week, as a summary.

options.label: The spec requires the tester's raw files for every link and a witnessed sample — at least one in ten, and every long or unusual run — and pulling plans must state tension limits
options.result: Bram circulates it to every cabling trade; the fiber sub sends raw files unprompted.
options.consequence: Evidence you can trace, and a witness.

options.label: Maya witnesses every test herself
options.consequence: Not her role — and not scalable.

options.label: Drop certification; just check the screens work
options.result: The first marginal link fails in winter.

items.text: FIELD NOTE —  A certification summary proves nothing on its own: ask for the tester’s raw files and witness a sample. Crosstalk (NEXT) fails first when cable is damaged — kinked, crushed or pulled past its rated tension (ratio = applied ÷ rated). Installation methods are the installer’s; the spec sets the limits; the commissioning agent verifies.
REFLECTION (optional)  · Which “pass” at your work would you struggle to trace back to a real test?
